keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Gangavadi with Kongu, held "470: The Gangas gained control of the Kongu region and other areas" (the page also puts the start of Kongu control under Avinita in the 6th century). The page gives no later changes except the Rashtrakuta period (780-819, see the ledger) and says elsewhere that Ganga sovereignty lasted "from about 350 to 550 CE"; under Rashtrakuta suzerainty the Gangas were feudatories ("their loyal feudatory", Rashtrakuta page). Cliopatria draws this land as Kadamba (78 cells, 400-550), Chalukya, Pallava, Rashtrakuta (89-128 cells, 780-950) and Western Chalukya (105 cells, 990+). Review repair: 110 of the 205 cells of the 470 gain (and 121 of this shape's 375) lie in kalabhra-dynasty /keyframe_review/0-2, which holds them 353-601 with no loss to the Gangas; the 470 gain is now split so that the Kalabhra part names kalabhra-dynasty (confidence 1) and the rest stays nobody. The Chalukya (550-753) and Rashtrakuta (819-982) overlordships are vassal events in the ledger; the 780-819 Rashtrakuta hold is an occupation. Neither the Western Ganga nor the Kalabhra page says who held Kongu before 470.

ledger.note: c. 550: the Gangas become feudatories of the Badami Chalukyas. "The Western Ganga sovereignty lasted from about 350 to 550 CE" and "After the rise of the imperial Chalukyas of Badami, the Gangas accepted Chalukya overlordship and fought for the cause of their overlords against the Pallavas of Kanchi"; "the Gangas were feudatories and close allies who also shared matrimonial relations with the Chalukyas" (page, no year). The year is a bridge: 550 closes the page's sovereignty span and follows the Chalukya page's "established by Pulakeshin I in 543"; the Durvinita page (r. 529-579) calls his tie an alliance and friendship, not vassalage. Direction: this state is the vassal and the counterpart is the suzerain (the mirror the reviewer asked for); the schema names the vassal as counterpart, so chalukya-dynasty (sa-03) should carry vassal_start with counterpart western-ganga-dynasty.

ledger.note: 753: the Rashtrakutas replace the Badami Chalukyas. "The Chalukyas were replaced by the Rashtrakutas of Manyakheta in 753 CE as the dominant power in the Deccan" (Ganga page); the Rashtrakuta page has Dantidurga defeating Kirtivarman II in 753. The Ganga page adds that "the Gangas offered stiff resistance for about a century" after that. The year is the pages'; that the Ganga tie ended on that day is the researcher's reading.

ledger.note: 780: Rashtrakuta control of Gangavadi begins under Dhruva. "[Dhruva, who] took control in 780 ... also brought the Eastern Chalukyas and Gangas of Talakad under his control" (Rashtrakuta page, no year for the sentence); the Ganga page: Shivamara II's "defeat and imprisonment, his release from prison and eventually his death on the battle field", and "by 819, a Ganga resurgence gained them partial control over Gangavadi", so the Gangas had lost control of Gangavadi before 819. 780 is Dhruva's accession (his rule runs to 793); the Sripurusha page has the Ganga king ruling to 788 with "many victories against Krishna I", so the campaign may be later in the reign: a bridge. Replaces the first version's contest_start: the pages say the Gangas were brought under control, not that the field was shared. Direction: the owner's record with roles reversed (the occupier is the counterpart).

ledger.note: 819: a Ganga resurgence. "by 819, a Ganga resurgence gained them partial control over Gangavadi under King Rachamalla" (page); Amoghavarsha I "made peace with the Western Ganga dynasty by giving them his two daughters in marriage" (Rashtrakuta page, no year; his rule from 814, revolts suppressed by 821). The control regained is partial, so the hatching ends with the page's year.

ledger.note: 819 (bridge): the Gangas are Rashtrakuta feudatories after the peace. "their loyal feudatory, the Western Ganga Dynasty", "the vassal Ganga king Shivamara II", "the feudatory Western Ganga King Butuga II" (Rashtrakuta page, none dated); "The Gangas thereafter became staunch allies of the Rashtrakutas" (Ganga page, after Amoghavarsha I's gift of his daughter to Butuga I); Butuga II ascended in 938 "with the help of Rashtrakuta Amoghavarsha III" and Marasimha II (963) "aided the Rashtrakutas". The year is the resurgence of 819, the page's last date before the peace; the peace itself is undated within Amoghavarsha I's reign. Direction as in the 550 event: this state is the vassal.

No page opened says when the Gangas ceased to be feudatories: the Rashtrakuta page gives no year for Tailapa II's independence, and the Ganga page is silent on 973. wars.name: Rashtrakuta conquest of Gangavadi

wars.outcome: The Rashtrakutas under Dhruva (from 780) and Govinda III (793-814) bring Gangavadi under control, an occupation to 819; a Ganga resurgence regains partial control by 819 and Amoghavarsha I makes peace by marrying his daughters to the Gangas, who remain Rashtrakuta feudatories.
wars.note: No battle or year is given on the Rashtrakuta page, which is silent on a war by Dhruva or Govinda III against the Gangas and on the imprisonment of Shivamara II; 780 and 819 are the reign and resurgence years of the two pages. The ledger records the episode as an occupation (780-819), not a contest, after the review: the pages say the Gangas were "brought under control", not that the field was shared.

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks (sa-02-d asks for it as successor of the Pallavas). Three pages opened (budget 2-5). The life 350-999 spans the sa-03 period; sa-03 should add events if a page dates them (Chalukya of Badami suzerainty 6th-8th centuries, the Pallava war of Durvinita, Marasimha II's reign, Chavundaraya). Dates disagree: page says Ganga sovereignty "from about 350 to 550", infobox 350-1004, text "around the year 1000", Rajaraja page 998 and 1004; 999 is the last year of the last listed ruler (Rachamalla V 986-999). The Rashtrakuta episode is drawn as a contest 780-819 over Gangavadi because two pages date the Rashtrakuta takeover (780, 793-814) and the Ganga resurgence (819); afterwards the Gangas are feudatories, so rashtrakuta-dynasty (sa-03-d) should carry a vassal_start for western-ganga-dynasty from 819 to 973. The page's founder name (Konganivarma Madhava; infobox ruler Dadiga Madhava 350-370) and the multiple Rachamallas are unexplained, so no ruler strip. Cliopatria draws Gangavadi as Pallava (350), Kadamba (400-550), Chalukya (600-700), Pallava (700-800), Rashtrakuta (780-950), Western Chalukya (990-1004). Gazetteer names needed: Talakad, Kongu (region), Gangavadi (region), Manne, Channapatna; Hassan, Erode and Chamarajanagar are coordinate radii. REPAIR (2026-10-19, after review): the 470 gain is split (Kalabhra part names kalabhra-dynasty, confidence 1; the pages are silent on the former holder); vassal_start/vassal_end added for the Chalukyas (550-753, confidence 1/2) and the Rashtrakutas (819-982, confidence 1) in the vassal's-own-ledger direction (counterpart = suzerain); the 780-819 contest becomes an occupation (confidence 1/2). Thin gap 550-780 re-tried on the Durvinita, Sripurusha and Talakad pages: no event with a land change is dated (Durvinita r. 529-579 with the Anderi, Alattur, Porulare and Pernagra victories undated; Sripurusha r. 726-788, 731 victory over Nandivarman II with the place not given; his capital moved to Manne without a year; the Talakad page gives Harivarma 247-266 by the chronicle against the Ganga page's 390 and no year for the capital).
